remarks:
On bell: cartouche engraved with date “ 1612” and coats of arms of the Nuremberg patrician families Volckamer, Harsdörfer, Tetzel, Haller von Hallerstein, Starch, Nützel, Prünsteter.
Decorative flat slide-stays, hinged handle on lower slide-stay. Immoveable slide stay engraved on one side with a representation of Vanity (woman with arm resting on a skull), and on the other side the head of a putto with initials “I E”; dragon-head clasps on moveable slide stay; adjacent sleeves have on one side engraved soldier and a crowned head of a woman, on the other side a cast putto head. Cast-iron handle with ivory knob (of later date) attached to moveable slide stay. Flat bell-stay, plain, probably not orig., with eyelets on either end. Leaf-shaped hinge plate adjacent to bell-stay (on bell-pipe side) with engraved leaf pattern. Tubing looped twice in bell sec., with tuning slide, capable of lowering the pitch of the instrument by a step; long push-rod attached to tuning slide at end of loop. Stay connecting neck-pipe to opposite side of coil probably not original. Ring in slide bow; slide bow and bow preceding terminal bell section have cast ring with oblique ridges mounted on leaf-shaped plate with engraved leaf design. At the distal end of the knot-shaped bow on the tuning slide is a crown. In the knot are the three Nuremberg coats of arms within a wreath. Bell not strongly flared. Cast rim wire with braid; teeth perforated with small holes on inner border of garland. Ferrules (19 in all) and rim-wire silver-plated; putto-heads, dragon-head clasps, crown, coat of arms in knot in bell bow and grip on tuning slide rod are gold-plated. Some ferrules have wide border with oval plumes and other ornamental figures, herring-bone pattern in middle section, border on opposite end narrow with leaf pattern; others have oblique rings at borders and leaf-shaped notches. Two details of the instrument described by Wörthmüller in 1955 are now missing: a gold-plated knob with angel’s heads as grip for the rod on the tuning slide and a wire wreath attached with a leaf-shaped engraved piece of metal, surrounding a cast representation of the imperial two-headed eagle.
